story.title: Private social clubs: Dallas' new ‘third place for the wealthy'
story.summary: An influx of affluent newcomers and shifting demands from residents are fueling demand for members-only spaces where dining, socializing, and business mix. Gold-coated elevators bring clubgoers up to Park House in Highland Park Village, where concierges stand on checker-like flooring underneath a massive pink light fixture to check members and guests in. Not far away in Preston Hollow, 55 Seventy members talk business over lunch in a dimly lit dining room with brown and blue hues, their wine stored in lockers that line a 6,000-square-foot wine cellar set at 55 degrees and 70% humidity. For a growing swath who can afford it, Dallas-area private social clubs — Park House and 55 Seventy being the most popular — are where parties are thrown, business gets done, and dinners are enjoyed.
